# MFE Orchestrator

> Ship a micro frontend without rebuilding the host application.

MFE Orchestrator is an open-source control plane for micro frontends (MFEs). It
stores every build, decides which version each environment serves, and hands the
host application the runtime configuration it needs — including the Module
Federation wiring. Releasing a micro frontend therefore never requires
rebuilding or redeploying the shell, and a rollback is a version change rather
than a rebuild. It runs as a hosted console or self-hosted with Docker Compose.

Category: micro frontend deployment and orchestration platform.
Also written: micro-frontend, microfrontend. MFE stands for micro frontend.

Key capabilities: version registry per environment (DEV/UAT/PROD and custom),
runtime configuration for Module Federation hosts under Webpack and Vite, canary
releases with gradual traffic shifting, one-step rollback, artifact storage on
AWS S3 / Azure Blob Storage / Google Cloud Storage / on-premise, and CI/CD
integrations for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Azure DevOps.

This file is a pointer. The documentation is served under /documentation and
carries its own llms.txt, which indexes every page.

## Concepts

- [What is a micro frontend (MFE)?](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/what-is-a-micro-frontend): definition of the term, the architecture, its trade-offs and when it is worth adopting
- [Module Federation versioning and dynamic remotes](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/module-federation): why Module Federation alone leaves version selection to you, and how the orchestrator replaces a hand-maintained remotes file
- [FAQ](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/faq): what MFE stands for, how orchestration differs from plain Module Federation, versioning, canary releases, rollback and self-hosting
- [Get started](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/start-now): the hosted console, or self-hosting with Docker Compose
- [Why we built it](https://mfe-orchestrator.dev/about): the release problem that led to the project
